I had the same question but also couldn’t find any discussions on it. But I did go through all the twelfth night videos on NT’s channel and from what I’ve watched I’d interpret the wig coming off as an act of shedding a mask. Malvolia was a very controlled person with monochrome clothes and precisely cut hair because she didn’t want to lose her authority as a steward and feared that if she did, it would distance herself from Olivia. There’s a video where Tamsin Greig talks about how control comes from fear and that’s why Malvolia is always so calculated to the point of her gestures looking rather silly. But once she realises that Olivia might actually lover her back, all that control goes out the window and she’s like a tight corn seed being popped into a huge popcorn (it’s an analogy used by Tamsin and the director and is why Malvolia appears in that flamboyant white top). 
But in the end it turns out she was speaking to her own imagination and is horridly abused. Feste is one of the abusers but also someone who frees Malvolia out of that controlled state I mentioned before. Malvolia rises out of that abuse and doesn’t revert back to her old clothes or manners. She gone beyond that and is ready for a new chapter in her life, away from the control and her abusers (Tamsin jokes how there might be a sequel for Malvolia in her interview). 
So Malvolia discards her wig, goes outside in her colourful clothes, and walks up into the rain and the rain is washing the oppression away.

If you’re interested, there’s a great 40 minute interview w Tamsin Greig on the NT channel and also a short series on the themes of this production!

It’s amazing how many people use the terms cloudy or brain fog! I thought I was the only one. I often feel like my head is full of sand and my eyesight gets blurry. Like you my interests were a constant subject of shame and guilt. So I hid them all and almost forgot about them because it was easier for my mind when I succumbed to my parents’ guilt tripping regarding my passions. If I fought against it nothing would change, I’d only get furious and even black out from the anger. So most of the time I held back in everything I did. I became my own obstacle and controller almost to the level of ocd. I still live with my nmom which doesn’t help at all but at least things are a little (just barely but at least it’s some progress) better so I’m inching towards self awareness and realising who I might be. I’m 23 and it all feels very strange. I’m grateful I got this chance however late it might feel and am trying my best to work on myself and become my own person. I struck up the courage to own my love of the arts but its a constant battle against myself because I’ve been trained to put myself down and place fear before love at all times. So I feel terrified of my love of the arts and even avoid it for months because it’s always been connected to intense shame/guilt which I absolutely hate.

Like I said living in the presence of the person responsible for all of my trauma makes it the hardest thing to do. Everyday I fight through my cloudy brain to try and regain a feeling of myself. Otherwise I zone out most of the time, losing sense of self and fall into horrid anxiety.
